stem: Let f(x) = sin(2x). What is the average rate of change of f on the interval [0, π/4]?

rationales.A: Average rate of change = (f(π/4) - f(0))/(π/4 - 0) = (sin(π/2) - sin(0))/(π/4) = (1 - 0)/(π/4) = 4/π.
rationales.B: Sign reversed: computing (f(0) - f(π/4))/(π/4) = (0 - 1)/(π/4) gives -4/π. The later value must be subtracted first.
rationales.C: Did not divide by the interval length: f(π/4) - f(0) = 1 - 0 = 1 is the change in f, not its average rate of change.
rationales.D: Dropped the coefficient inside the argument: using sin(π/4) - sin(0) = √2/2 instead of sin(2·π/4) - sin(0), then dividing by π/4, gives 2√2/π.

misconception_map.B: Subtracts in the wrong order, so the sign is reversed
misconception_map.C: Gives the change in the function without dividing by the interval length
misconception_map.D: Drops the coefficient inside the argument when evaluating, for example using the value at x instead of at kx

stem: Let g(x) = 3cos(2x) + 1. What is the average rate of change of g on the interval [π/6, 5π/6]?

rationales.A: g(π/6) = 3cos(π/3) + 1 = 5/2 and g(5π/6) = 3cos(5π/3) + 1 = 5/2. So (g(5π/6) - g(π/6))/(5π/6 - π/6) = 0/(2π/3) = 0. The function is not constant on the interval; its values at the two endpoints are equal.
rationales.B: Used an instantaneous rate at the left endpoint: the derivative -6sin(2x) at x = π/6 is -6sin(π/3) = -3√3, which is not the average rate of change.
rationales.C: Used an instantaneous rate at the right endpoint: the derivative -6sin(2x) at x = 5π/6 is -6sin(5π/3) = 3√3, which is not the average rate of change.
rationales.D: Dropped the coefficient inside the argument: using 3cos(x) + 1 gives (3cos(5π/6) - 3cos(π/6))/(2π/3) = (-3√3)/(2π/3) = -9√3/(2π).

stem: The height of a weight bouncing on a spring is modeled by h(t) = 12 + 5sin(2t) centimeters, where t is the time in seconds. What is the average rate of change of h over the time interval π/6 ≤ t ≤ π/2?

rationales.B: Used an instantaneous rate at the midpoint: the derivative 10cos(2t) at t = π/3 is 10cos(2π/3) = -5, giving -5 cm per second, which is the rate at one instant, not the average over the interval.
rationales.C: Sign reversed: computing (h(π/6) - h(π/2))/(π/3) = (5√3/2)/(π/3) gives 15√3/(2π) cm per second. The later value must be subtracted first.
rationales.D: Did not divide by the interval length: h(π/2) - h(π/6) = -5√3/2 is the change in height in centimeters, so -5√3/2 cm per second is not the average rate of change.

stem:
The table gives selected values of a function f.

x: 0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9
f(x): 1, 10, 16, 28, 24, 26

On which of the following intervals is the average rate of change of f greatest?

rationales.B: Divided by the right endpoint instead of the interval length: (10 - 1)/2 = 9/2 on [0, 2] beats (16 - 10)/3 = 2 on [2, 3], so [0, 2] looks greatest. The divisor must be b - a.
rationales.C: Compared function values at the right endpoints: f(9) = 26 is the largest right-endpoint value, so [7, 9] was chosen, but its average rate of change is only (26 - 24)/2 = 1.
rationales.D: Used the mean of the endpoint values: (28 + 24)/2 = 26 on [5, 7] is the largest mean, so [5, 7] was chosen, but its average rate of change is (24 - 28)/2 = -2.

misconception_map.B: Divides by the right endpoint instead of the interval length
misconception_map.C: Compares function values at the right endpoints instead of rates
misconception_map.D: Uses the mean of the two endpoint values (an average value of the function) instead of the average rate of change

stem: The volume of water in a reservoir is modeled by V(t) = 40√(t + 1) - 4t thousand cubic meters, where t is the time in days, 0 ≤ t ≤ 35. On which of the following intervals is the average rate of change of V least?

rationales.B: Compared function values at the right endpoints: V(8) = 88 is the smallest right-endpoint value, so [3, 8] was chosen, but its average rate of change is 4 thousand cubic meters per day.
rationales.C: Divided by the right endpoint instead of the interval length: (100 - 88)/15 = 4/5 on [8, 15] is smaller than (100 - 68)/35 = 32/35 on [3, 35], so [8, 15] was chosen, but its average rate of change is 12/7 thousand cubic meters per day.
rationales.D: Used the mean of the endpoint values: (40 + 100)/2 = 70 on [0, 15] is the smallest mean, so [0, 15] was chosen, but its average rate of change is 4 thousand cubic meters per day.
